newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrican SIH buys 10 pct in SMG from Dato'Samsudin.
newsitem.headline: SAfrican SIH buys 10 pct in SMG from Dato'Samsudin.

text.p: SANCO Investment Holdings (SIH) has bought a 10 percent stake in SMG Holdings for about 25 million rand from Malaysian businessman Dato'Samsudin Abu Hassan.
The deal, announced Tuesday by Dato'Samsudin's New Republic Bank Ltd, will cut Dato's shareholding in SMG to 64 percent.

SANCO is South Africa's largest community-based organisation with more than 1.2 million members. "Through The New Republic Bank Ltd and SANCO, people at the very grass-roots of South African society will be empowered in terms of financial services," Dato'Samsudin said in a statement.
In separate statements Dato announced two further deals, including the sale by Dato'Samsudin of property firm Denprop Ltd to SMG for 8.5 million rand cash.

SMG has also acquired 9,986,585 shares in property development group Samrand for 14.5 million rand from Baxley Securities Ltd. Baxley, in turn, has agreed to buy 3,900,000 shares in The New Republic Bank from SMG for 16.8 million rand.
The deal leaves SMG with a 7.9 percent stake in Samrand. "SMG intends to increase its investment in Samrand in due course," the firm said.
